short: First intracranial decoder of imagined whole words (M08, ahead within ECoG); DTW kernel (M06) new but its gain unquantified; no control for the trace of the just-heard word.
position: The paper changes two components of intracranial imagined-speech decoding [@martin2016word]. Whole-word identity as the decoded unit (M08) is ahead: none of the 4 earlier intracranial imagined-speech decoders classifies words (Appendix), and imagined word pairs beat chance in 4 of 5 subjects. DTW inside the SVM kernel (M06) is new in this population (Appendix) but standard by rule, because its gain is reported only as an unpaired test with no stated unit or size. The test partition (M12) is the usual within-participant cross-validation. The strongest confound is the heard word: the imagery epoch follows the auditory stimulus, and no same-delay epoch without imagery separates imagery from its trace. The "first demonstration of single-trial neural decoding of words during imagined speech" holds only for intracranial recordings; Suppes et al. recognised single internal-speech trials from scalp EEG/MEG in 1997 [@suppes1997brain].
